note: Systemic beta-blockers; stopping suddenly can cause rebound angina, tachycardia or infarction. Eye drops (S01ED) are not on the list.
Antiepileptics; stopping suddenly can trigger seizures or status epilepticus. The old gabapentinoid codes in this group (N03AX12, N03AX16) are listed separately under gabapentinoid.

Systemic corticosteroids (glucocorticoids and fludrocortisone); stopping suddenly after long use can cause adrenal crisis. Skin (D07), inhaled (R03BA), nasal (R01AD), eye (S01BA) and gut-acting (A07EA) forms are not on the list. Gut-acting corticosteroids (A07EA) are not added (owner decision 2026-11-07: low systemic exposure).
Benzodiazepines (anxiolytic); stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal seizures and delirium.
Benzodiazepines (hypnotic); same withdrawal risk.
Clonazepam; same withdrawal risk (also covered by the antiepileptic group).
Tetrazepam, a benzodiazepine coded as a muscle relaxant (withdrawn in the EU); same withdrawal risk.
Antidepressants; stopping suddenly can cause discontinuation syndrome, and with MAO inhibitors and tricyclics severe rebound effects.
Clonidine (tablets and patches); stopping suddenly can cause rebound hypertensive crisis.
Clonidine coded for migraine prevention; same rebound risk.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Other centrally acting alpha-2 agonists (guanfacine, moxonidine, rilmenidine); rebound hypertension after a sudden stop is described, less often than with clonidine.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Lofexidine; its label advises gradual reduction because blood pressure rebounds after a sudden stop.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Gabapentin, pregabalin, mirogabalin; sudden withdrawal can cause seizures (in people with epilepsy) and withdrawal symptoms; labels advise tapering over at least a week.
Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Old gabapentin code still published by TİTCK.
Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Old pregabalin code still published by TİTCK.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Baclofen; sudden withdrawal can cause hallucinations, seizures and, after intrathecal use, a life-threatening syndrome.
Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Tizanidine; sudden withdrawal can cause rebound hypertension and tachycardia.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Opioid analgesics; sudden stop in a physically dependent person causes withdrawal; the FDA warned in 2019 of serious harm after sudden opioid stops in dependent patients.
Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Opioids for opioid dependence (methadone, buprenorphine); same risk.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Levodopa and other dopaminergic drugs; sudden withdrawal can cause a neuroleptic-malignant-like syndrome and severe worsening of parkinsonism.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Antipsychotics; sudden withdrawal can cause rebound psychosis, withdrawal dyskinesia and, with clozapine, cholinergic rebound.
Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Lithium; sudden stop raises the risk of early relapse of mania.

Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Z-drugs (zolpidem, zopiclone); rebound insomnia, and withdrawal seizures after high doses.
Beyond the examples of medical-safety.md rule 4; confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (over-inclusion is the safe side). Barbiturate hypnotics; sudden withdrawal can cause seizures and delirium.

Codeine as an antitussive: Wikidata gives codeine only R05DA04, so without this row codeine would get no opioid warning; a physically dependent person can have withdrawal after a sudden stop. Added by the owner on 2026-11-07.
